stem: An industrial engineering study measures the assembly time (seconds) for a sample of 25 factory workers. The sample mean is 116.0 sec with a sample standard deviation of 40.3 sec. However, 3 of the 25 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 22 observations have a mean of 110.5 sec and standard deviation of 28.9 sec. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 116.0, 95% CI = [99.4, 132.6]. Without outliers: mean = 110.5, 95% CI = [98.2, 122.8]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [98.2, 132.6]. Point estimate: 113.2 sec.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [98.2, 132.6].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
